changes: p1 Nīlakavi: removed role 'author' — the Sanskrit text is presented as spoken by Rudra (rudreṇoktam); Nīlakavi made the vernacular bhāṣāṭīkā, so the role is commentator. Kept donor because he offers the book to the king (arpitaṃ pustakaṃ)
p1: removed title 'kavi' — it is written as part of the compound name nīlakavinā; whether it means 'the poet Nīla' is mentioned in notes
p1: scribe role not added, since the colophon does not say he copied the manuscript (the catalogue says it does); see notes
p2: name normalized to the regnal form Rājendravikrama Śāha, with confidence changed from high to medium because the reading rājendrādimavikrama is garbled
date: added the reign range in notes; no explicit date

purpose: offered with devotion (bhaktyārpitam?) to King Rājendravikrama
notes: The colophon has no date. If the king is Rājendra Vikrama Śāha of Nepal, the manuscript would date from about 1816–1847 CE. 'rājendrādimavikramāya' is garbled; it probably stands for Rājendra(-ādima?)vikrama, and the catalogue reads Rājendravikrama Śāha. 'bhavatyārpitaṃ' is probably an error for 'bhaktyārpitaṃ' (offered with devotion). 'gairīya bhāṣā' presumably means the hill language, i.e. Nepali (Gorkhālī/Parbatiyā). 'prasastam' should read 'praśastam'. Nīlakavi made the Nepali bhāṣāṭīkā on the Rudrākṣamāhātmya, which comes from the Tantracintāmaṇi, and presented it to the king. The catalogue lists him as the scribe, but the colophon only shows him as the commentator who offered the book; this copy may be his own autograph presentation copy. 'kavi' may be a title (the poet Nīla) rather than part of the name.
